newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London mixed, expiry dulls trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London mixed, expiry dulls trade.

text.p: U.S. stocks were mixed in quiet trading on Friday, with sentiment dampened by a lacklustre close on Wall Street and the "triple witching" expiry of options and futures on shares and share indices in the U.S.

"This is a very divided market and things are quiet at the moment. We see it staying that way -- people are a little concerned about the expiry producing some swings so they're playing safe at the moment," one trader said.
Modest business focused on high-technology stocks, which had outperformed the generally dull Wall Street market. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed 0.16 percent lower.

Dealers said the Dow was likely to remain flat on Friday but said some swings were possible because of the expiry. "The tone remains uninspired and picky...and of course the FOMC meeting is coming up" a dealer said.
Among hi-tech stocks in London, Micron was up $3/4 at $28-1/8 and Microsoft Corp was down $1/4 at $137-1/2.

General Motors Corp. was down $1/8 at $48-1/2 on what one dealer called indecision about the pricing of the car giant's new mini-vans. Prices were set higher than competing models from Chrysler Corp. and Ford Motor Co..
